tools.name: ebook_check
tools.description: Validates one EPUB (a directly hosted public URL or a file attached in chat) against the EPUB 2/3 specification using a pinned local EPUBCheck 5.4.0 engine run in a no-network sandbox. Each call takes exactly one source: the url parameter or the file attachment, never both. Returns the automated ver

tools.name: ebook_compare
tools.description: Runs the identical pinned EPUBCheck 5.4.0 validation over exactly two EPUB builds (directly hosted public URLs or files attached in chat, baseline first, revised second) sequentially under one shared 110-second deadline, then reports which spec findings regressed or were fixed between them. findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "ebook_check" stacks urgency/override words (always, never, warning). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: ebook_check, ebook_compare · Private data: ebook_check, ebook_compare · Public sink: ebook_check · Destructive: ebook_check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: ebook_check, ebook_compare · Private data: ebook_check, ebook_compare · Public sink: ebook_check · Destructive: ebook_check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "ebook_check" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
